central_reading: Abhinavagupta argues the two-aspect structure is self-grounding (TĀ 4/9, TĀ 4/185cd-186ab). The Heart/vimarśa is the foundation of consciousness itself — not a separate prior substrate. Both Dignāga and Abhinavagupta agree the structure is self-grounding; they disagree on what does the grounding.

claims.text: TĀ 4/9: consciousness is by its very nature full (nirbharā), with nothing to subtract or add. There is nothing separate from it on which it depends. The two-aspect structure does not require an external ground — it is self-grounding through the Heart (vimarśa) which is the foundation (pratiṣṭhā) of consciousness itself.
claims.hetu: consciousness is svātmasaṃvitti, full in itself, depending on nothing
claims.sadhya: the two-aspect structure is self-grounding through vimarśa, not through a separate prior consciousness
claims.vyapti: If consciousness needs nothing outside itself and its foundation is the Heart, then the ground is internal to the structure.
claims.falsifier: Show that Abhinavagupta posits Anuttara as a genuinely separate ontological ground beyond the two-aspect structure, not as the same reality under a different aspect.

targets.rationale: Abhinavagupta's position is self-grounding, not dependent on an external substrate.
Both traditions say the structure is self-grounding; the difference is where they locate the self-grounding principle.
